- When sentiment is high (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.4–0.8); apply smoothing or lagged mean reversion.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong downward sentiment + price decline, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; forecast should be slightly above recent low.  
- When sentiment is uniformly high over 5+ days, model tends to overfit upward trend; apply downward bias of 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
